title: Reporting Queries, Indexes, JDBC Project and Review
description: Reporting queries with subqueries, common table expressions and window functions for top-N-per-group, indexes and reading query plans with EXPLAIN; the F23 JDBC data access project, which connects Java to PostgreSQL and replaces an in-memory repository with a JDBC one; then the course review pages for SQL and for JDBC.
sourceCoverageNotes: Second-mate grouping decision, not syllabus: calendar day F22 (/tracks/0/weeks/4/days/1, rows 0-3, relation exact) and the two F24 review rows (/tracks/0/weeks/4/days/3, rows 0-1, kind review, relation exact).

F23 'JDBC data access' is a Project day: its five rows (/tracks/0/weeks/4/days/2, rows 0-4) are one project row, delivered as one canonical project artifact, jdbc-data-access-project (kind lab-brief): a learner-facing project brief with a topic coding lab (starter scaffold and public tests). Captain decision pep-project-rows option A (reconciliation sql-intake-edu-001). The Standard and Fast overlays reuse this artifact by reference and never duplicate it.

jdbc-data-access-project teaches the JDBC concepts no earlier page covers (connecting through pgJDBC, prepared statements and SQL injection, transactions and ACID, testing against a test database) in its own brief instruction; jdbc-review retrieves them on F24 and adds no new syllabus.
F24 row 2 'SQL module check' is the course assessment blueprint assessments/sql-module-check, not a topic.

Planned module coding lab (lab plan in workflow/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/intake.md): subquery, CTE and top-N-per-group window queries tested with mvn -q -o test against a lab-created database on the learner-local PostgreSQL server through pgJDBC (no container); authored with its lab.json in the reporting-indexes-and-review module PR, so moduleLabs stays empty until the lab exists.
